title: Reconstruct an Incident from Business and Technical Evidence
summary: Build an evidence-based incident timeline and choose corrective actions that address the demonstrated failure mechanism.
prerequisites: Understand event publication stages, asynchronous processing, and idempotency.
Be able to read a sanitized execution or integration log.
learningObjectives: Distinguish symptom, contributing condition, and demonstrated cause.
Correlate publication, delivery, and business completion.
Write a useful post-incident review with testable actions.

sections.heading: Begin with the customer outcome
body: Irina did not receive a test-drive notification. Oleg sees a successful booking and a log message saying 'event published.' These facts do not establish that a notification provider received or delivered anything. Define the missing business outcome before searching for the most dramatic error line.

Observability means having enough useful signals to understand what the system did and why. Logs describe individual events, metrics summarize behavior over time, and traces connect stages of an execution. None is sufficient alone. A low error count can coexist with missing work if the code never attempted the relevant stage or logged success too early.

callouts.text: The first incident question is 'What outcome is missing for whom?' rather than 'Which log looks suspicious?'

sections.heading: Follow the stages and their acknowledgments
body: Platform Event publication is asynchronous. A successful SaveResult from EventBus.publish reports the intermediate queuing result, not the final publication result or a subscriber's business completion. Publish callbacks can report the final publication outcome for supported events, but even publication success does not prove that an external provider completed its work.

The synthetic timeline below shows a mismatch between the dashboard's definition of success and the actual process. The subscriber attempted a provider call, timed out, and recorded no durable recovery state. The evidence supports a lost unresolved outcome; it does not prove whether the provider delivered the message before the timeout.

Keep timestamp sources explicit. Browser, Salesforce, and provider clocks can differ, and logs can arrive late. Use operation identifiers and causal relationships where possible rather than relying only on apparently adjacent timestamps. Preserve uncertainty when a stage lacks evidence.

callouts.text: Give each acknowledgment a precise meaning: queued, published, consumed, provider accepted, or business outcome confirmed.

codeBlocks.caption: Synthetic incident evidence
codeBlocks.code:
09:00:00 Booking A-101 committed
09:00:01 Publisher SaveResult isSuccess=true; dashboard marks Notified
09:00:03 Subscriber starts notification operation N-77
09:00:05 Provider request times out; no durable retry item recorded
09:30:00 Irina reports no message
Unknown: whether the provider accepted N-77 before the timeout
Known defect: dashboard marked success before downstream confirmation

sections.heading: Separate recovery from causal explanation
body: The immediate recovery task is to reconcile N-77 with the provider or apply the approved idempotent retry procedure. Blindly sending a new notification with a new operation key can create duplicates. The incident explanation is a separate task: why did an uncertain outcome disappear, and why did the dashboard misreport it?

A cause statement should connect a mechanism to evidence. 'The developer was careless' explains neither the status transition nor the missing recovery state. A stronger statement identifies that code used the queuing acknowledgment as a completed-notification signal and did not persist timeout handling. Contributing conditions might include a test suite that covered only successful responses.

An action such as 'be more careful' is not verifiable. Better actions include separating notification states, adding a timeout test, persisting recovery work, monitoring old Pending items, and assigning an owner to the reconciliation procedure. Each action needs a completion test and a responsible role.

callouts.text: Write corrective actions as observable changes with an owner and a verification method.

sections.heading: Measure the process that can fail silently
body: Add counts and age distributions for Pending notifications, attempts, confirmed provider acknowledgments, and unresolved outcomes. Alerting thresholds should reflect the business tolerance and observed normal behavior. Do not invent a universal threshold from this fictional incident.

For longer interruptions, remember that an event bus is not an unlimited archive. Standard Platform Event and CDC retention is limited, and recovery beyond the available replay window may require reconciliation from durable business state. A checkpoint is useful, but it does not replace a recovery source.

Your classroom submission can be a timeline, an evidence table, and a test proposal. Clearly mark supplied statements as synthetic and distinguish inference from proof. You do not need to manufacture a production outage to demonstrate disciplined incident reasoning.

callouts.text: An unexplained gap is a finding. Do not fill it with a confident story that the available evidence cannot support.

exercise.title: Write a short Northstar incident review
exercise.brief: Explain the synthetic N-77 notification incident and propose a safe recovery and prevention plan.
steps: Create a timeline with evidence source, event, known consequence, and uncertainty.
State the customer impact without assuming the provider's unknown outcome.
Describe an idempotent reconciliation or retry path for N-77.
Write two demonstrated causes or design defects and separate them from hypotheses.
Create three corrective actions with owners, tests, and a signal that would detect recurrence.
acceptance: The report distinguishes queuing success from downstream completion.
The timeout remains an uncertain remote outcome until reconciled.
Corrective actions can be verified and avoid blame-only explanations.
exercise.stretch: Explain how recovery changes if the subscriber has been offline beyond the event retention window.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does EventBus.publish SaveResult success prove?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It reports successful queuing of the publish operation, not final publication or subscriber completion.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why not resend with a new notification key immediately?
knowledgeCheck.answer: The first call may have completed remotely despite the timeout; a new key can create a second business effect.

knowledgeCheck.question: What makes a corrective action useful?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It changes an identified failure mechanism, has a responsible owner, and includes a concrete verification or recurrence-detection method.

recap: Trace the missing business outcome through distinct acknowledgments.
Turn causal findings into owned and testable improvements.
